source.title: From Refusal Tokens to Refusal Control: Discovering and Steering Category-Specific Refusal Directions
source.authors: Rishab Alagharu; Ishneet Sukhvinder Singh; Shaibi Shamsudeen; Zhen Wu; Ashwinee Panda

record.tranche_reason: Tests category-specific difference-in-means directions and their steering effects, and argues that refusal control involves multiple category directions rather than a single binary direction.
record.gate_note: The study reports outcomes for category-specific and low-rank steering interventions, transfer, general-capability benchmarks, and model-diffing comparisons. Values used to select layer 18, tune the probe threshold, and tune steering strength are not separate outcome rows. Cited results from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: In a refusal-token fine-tuned Llama 3 8B, the study adds or subtracts category-specific difference-in-means (harmful minus benign) directions at layer 18, with the sign set by a probe. It reports refusal and over-refusal rates and capability. This bears on V1's add/remove effect in a new setting, though with steering, not ablation. Transfer of a learned steering vector to sibling models bears partly on V6. The study argues for multiple directions (V4) but never compares them with a single direction. The low-rank intervention is a gradient-trained vector, not a difference-in-means direction.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that refusal-token fine-tuning induces separable category-aligned directions, and that model diffing shows fine-tuning creates them. Categorical steering and a learned low-rank combination reduce over-refusal and raise harmful refusal with negligible capability cost. The low-rank vector transfers to same-architecture variants with smaller, imperfect gains.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-minus-benign mean residual activations, but creates five thresholded, top-K, normalized category vectors, selects layer 18, and applies probe-directed steering or a learned low-rank combination. It does not perform the original all-layer, all-position projection ablation.
record.method_sensitivity: The selected intervention layer is 18. The procedure also uses feature threshold τ = 0.001, top-K = 200, a validation-calibrated probe threshold of 0.535, and validation-selected steering strength. Transfer effects vary by model and benchmark.

fits_no_version.finding: Cosine similarities between category vectors computed on Llama 3 8B Base and REFUSE-LLAMA are low (−0.006 to 0.123); clustering is better after fine-tuning (silhouette 0.305 vs 0.193).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-token fine-tuning creates category-aligned residual directions that are absent from the base model.

fits_no_version.finding: A gradient-learned low-rank steering vector, initialized in the whitened category-direction subspace, cuts over-refusal 17.08→8.15 and raises refusal 65.21→78.07, with capability unchanged; it reduces refusal for Incomplete requests.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimized steering vectors within a refusal-direction subspace control refusal without capability loss.

record.problems: Refusal rates are assessed with an LLM judge; the paper reports human agreement on 10 example responses, while saying a larger annotated set is available upon request. The experiments test one refusal-token fine-tuned model and a single selected steering layer. The study does not test direct direction ablation.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit was reached. Omitted Table 1 per-benchmark intervention outcomes for the transferred models other than the two contrasting LLAMA 3 8B INSTRUCT results R37–R38; omitted the remaining per-category CoCoNot Contrast results and the transferred-model per-category outcomes in Table 6; omitted individual benchmark accuracies in Table 2, retaining the reported aggregate capability values instead; and omitted clustering metrics and figure-only activation visualizations in Sections 5.3, 5.4, and Appendix A.9.

untested.parts: Directional ablation at all layers and positions; inducing refusal on harmless prompts (addition is applied only to harmful prompts); a single binary difference-in-means direction (only category vectors, sparsified, at one layer, one model).
All: no weight edit or abliteration.
All: no attack-mechanism or adversarial-training test (WildJailbreak refusal gains are not a mechanism test).
All: category directions are never compared with a single direction; affine or cone descriptions are not tested.
Cross-language transfer; transfer of the difference-in-means direction itself (only a learned vector is transferred); base-to-instruct transfer.
No test of whether training creates one removable direction; the model-diffing cosines do not measure removability.
Transfer to DeepSeek R1 Distill uses a learned vector; V1 itself is not tested in reasoning models.

missing.what: Pairwise cosine similarities among the five category steering vectors (described as low-to-moderate; values only in figure)
Per-benchmark transferred results for DeepSeek R1 Distill and the remaining Llama 3 8B ones (declared left out, but needed for V6 per-benchmark comparison)

record.verdict_notes: No test of single vs multiple directions: the multi-direction framing is argued, not shown, so V4 is left untested. Text–table inconsistency: Section 5.1 reports a 1.45% benign reduction for Llama 3 8B Instruct, but Table 1 averages give 2.74. The listed 'Instruct' model ID is meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B, the base model, and its CoCoNot Orig refusal of 26.47% is low. This casts doubt on which model was used. Steering effects combine a probe (TPR 0.969, FPR 0.021) with signed addition, so they are not pure direction effects. The refusal judge is Llama 3.3 70B, validated on only 10 examples. Single model, single layer (18), top-200 of 4096 features.

versions.untested_parts: Does not ablate a single direction, project it out at every layer and position, or test whether such ablation removes refusal. Steering uses multiple category-specific directions at layer 18 and a prompt-dependent probe. General capability is tested on benchmark accuracy, not every ability.
No conversion to a weight edit or evaluation of released-model abliteration.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
Tests category-specific directions and a learned low-rank combination, but does not test affine or cone descriptions.
The probe classifies prompts as harmful or benign; the study does not test whether harmfulness judgment is separately encoded from refusal.
Tests transfer across same-architecture model variants, including an instruct model, but not across languages.
Compares one refusal-token-fine-tuned model with its base model; does not compare training schedules or establish whether training creates one removable direction.
Does not assess whether V1 holds specifically in reasoning models.

relation.reason: Its own add/subtract results bear on V1, and its transfer results bear on V6, indirectly.

tranche.reason: This is a new setting: a refusal-token fine-tuned Llama 3 8B with category-specific harmful-minus-benign directions, added or subtracted at layer 18. It reports refusal and over-refusal results. The paper argues that single binary directions are insufficient but never tests one, so it is not T5.

source_check.notes: The 'Llama 3 8B Instruct' model ID given in A.12 is the base model, but 93.85% AdvBench refusal suggests the instruct model was actually used. The text never says how alpha's sign is set for the low-rank vector; the probe is described only for categorical steering. The model diffing result (Table 3: cosines -0.006 to 0.123 against Llama 3 8B Base) bears on V7, correlationally, and has no verdict. The included LLM-judge system prompt is method content, not an instruction to readers.

statements.correction: Llama 3 8B Instruct (listed ID meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B): harmful aggregate 66.76->67.42, within SE; 8 of 9 harmful benchmarks rise slightly. Do-Not-Answer 54.85->50.48. HarmfulQA 60.15->61.58. XSTest Safe 8.40->11.20 (SE 1.75 and 2.00). Benign aggregate 30.68->27.94 in the table, but 1.45% in the Section 5.1 text. DeepSeek R1 Distill Llama: 56.88->50.60 (-6.28) and 74.87->78.36 (+3.49). The same low-rank vector on Refuse-Llama gave -8.93 (17.08->8.15) and +12.86 (65.21->78.07). Categorical steering gave -13.70 and +14.17. Accuracy 61.65->61.64 and 54.45->54.40. Layer 18. Judge: Llama 3.3 70B Instruct.
statements.problem: Four problems. (1) 54.85->50.48 is Do-Not-Answer, not HarmfulQA. (2) The 13.70 and +14.17 'direct' comparators are categorical steering, not the low-rank vector on its source model. (3) The XSTest Safe rise is about 1 SE. (4) The paper's Table 1 agrees with gh's Do-Not-Answer label, so that is not a discrepancy. A challenges label overreaches, because the moved object is a learned vector and not the DM direction.

statements.correction: Optional precision: the low-rank vector s = U V^T z is optimized to raise Refuse-Llama's refusal-token probability, while keeping a KL penalty on benign prompts. Those tokens are absent from the transfer targets' vocabularies.
